newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY AS INDIA DRAW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY AS INDIA DRAW.

text.p: Opener Navjot Sidhu scored a century to stake his claim for a place in Saturday's first test against Sri Lanka as India drew their three-day warm-up against a Board President's XI on Thursday.
Sidhu followed his first innings half-century with an unbeaten 100 enabling India to finish at 255 for five.
The tall, bearded Sikh, who scored a double century against West Indies in the Port-of-Spain test early this year, took 282 minutes and 191 balls. He hit 11 fours and two sixes.
Saurav Ganguly also used the opportunity to gain some valuable batting practice with an attractive 62.
He hit two sixes and seven fours in his 84-ball knock and shared a 125-run fourth wicket partnership with Sidhu.
India opened with wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia who is expected to play a similar role in the test. He was caught behind for 15 while attempting an ambitious pull.
Earlier, Abey Kuruvila and Debashish Mohanty wrapped up the Sri Lanka first innings for 291 by claiming the last three wickets for four runs off four deliveries.
